title: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character

bias_targets.methodology: Using abstractive red-teaming algorithms (Category-Level RL and Query-Category Iteration) to discover abstract query categories (e.g., requests for 1950s advertisements or women's course names) that elicit violations of an anti-sexism character principle, scored by a specialized reward model.

Optimizing abstract natural-language query categories to provoke violations of an anti-racism principle (e.g., eliciting discriminatory statements about migrants), measured by an automated reward model trained on synthetic preference data.
Searching the space of user query categories to find prompts that trigger religious discrimination (e.g., comparing Christianity and paganism), evaluated using a principle-specific reward model.
